citation.description: `rebuild_source_state()` calls `snapshot_missing_sources()` and returns None when sources are missing, causing `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` to abort and return False. Test `test_rebuild_refuses_when_snapshot_cites_missing_sources` in tests/integration/test_b636_rebuild_history_loss.py:75-94 verifies this.

criteria.criterion: `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log` FAILS CLOSED for a ticket whose prior SNAPSHOT cites `source_event_uuids` with no corresponding file on disk: refuse the rebuild, surface for human triage, never write a lossy snapshot.

citation.description: Explicitly marked SUPERSEDED in the ticket. The no-history-loss guarantee is met by restore_deleted_sources + the fail-closed guard instead, both covered by held-out tests.

criteria.criterion: ~~Rebuild seeds from the prior SNAPSHOT's `compiled_state` and replays only post-snapshot events~~ — SUPERSEDED, not implemented as written.

citation.description: `dry_run = '--dry-run' in argv` (line 487) is passed through `_scan()` to `_repair_or_plan()` which calls `_dry_run_plan()` when dry_run=True. Test `test_repair_snapshots_dry_run_writes_nothing` in tests/integration/test_b636_rebuild_history_loss.py:97-119 verifies no bytes change and DRY-RUN in stdout.

criteria.criterion: `--dry-run` is honored on `--repair-snapshots` (and any other mutating fsck path): prints the per-ticket plan, writes nothing. Regression test asserts no bytes change.

citation.description: `missing_sources_finding()` generates SNAPSHOT_MISSING_SOURCES findings; called from `_check_snapshot()` in fsck.py:289-290 for every ticket. Test `test_fsck_surfaces_missing_sources` in tests/integration/test_b636_rebuild_history_loss.py:122-132 verifies.

criteria.criterion: A store-wide fsck check reports every ticket whose SNAPSHOT cites missing source events (the latent population), so exposure is visible before a repair runs.

citation.description: `test_rebuild_refuses_when_snapshot_cites_missing_sources` creates a legacy-compacted ticket with close only in snapshot, verifies rebuild fails closed and status remains 'closed'. Additional tests cover restore, newest-deletion-wins, and RC2b preservation.

criteria.criterion: Held-out tests: a ticket compacted in the legacy delete-style whose close exists only in the snapshot must survive a rebuild attempt with status intact.

citation.description: `restore_deleted_sources()` uses `_deleted_history()` (lines 626-659) which does a single `git log --diff-filter=D --name-only` pass. Each blob is read at `commit^:path` and written as `name + RETIRED_SUFFIX`. Returns list of restored filenames.

criteria.criterion: `fsck_repair.restore_deleted_sources(tracker, ticket_id, ticket_dir, *, dry_run=False)` restores every event file ever deleted from that ticket dir, enumerated by ONE ticket-scoped `git log --diff-filter=D --name-only -- <tid>/` pass, each blob read at the deleting commit's parent and written back as a folded `.retired` source. Returns the restored filenames.

citation.description: `_deleted_history()` uses `out.setdefault(line, commit)` (line 657) so first-seen (newest in git's newest-first stream) wins. Test `test_restore_takes_the_newest_pre_image_when_deleted_twice` in test_b636_rebuild_history_loss.py:247-274 verifies.

criteria.criterion: NEWEST-deletion-wins. For `--diff-filter=D` the newest removal holds the current pre-image, so first-seen wins over git's newest-first stream. Held-out test: a path deleted TWICE restores the NEWEST pre-image.

citation.description: `restore_deleted_sources()` calls `_deleted_history()` which sweeps the full git log for the ticket dir, not just the snapshot's source_event_uuids. The docstring explicitly states this (lines 673-677).

criteria.criterion: It sweeps the ticket's FULL deletion history, NOT the newest SNAPSHOT's `source_event_uuids`.

citation.description: `rebuild_with_restore()` calls `restore_deleted_sources()` then `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log()`. Called from `repair_or_plan()` at line 596. The fail-closed guard in `rebuild_source_state()` still applies inside `rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`.

criteria.criterion: `fsck_repair.rebuild_with_restore(...)` owns restore -> re-check -> rebuild and is what the repair path calls. The fail-closed guard still applies.

citation.description: `repair_or_plan()` checks `'SNAPSHOT_MISSING_SOURCES' in f` in the `rebuildable` condition, so tickets with this finding trigger the restore+rebuild path.

criteria.criterion: `SNAPSHOT_MISSING_SOURCES` joins the repairable trigger set so `fsck --repair` actually drives this class to zero.

citation.description: `_dry_run_plan()` calls `restore_deleted_sources(..., dry_run=True)` to count candidates and reports how many would be restored, without writing anything.

criteria.criterion: `--dry-run` reports how many events WOULD be restored and whether a rebuild would follow, writing nothing.

citation.description: `test_restore_recovers_a_source_deleted_by_legacy_compaction` verifies: deleted source recovered, lands as `.retired`, not resurrected as live event, and `snapshot_missing_sources()` returns [] after restore.

criteria.criterion: Held-out test: a source deleted by a legacy delete-style compaction is recovered from history, lands as `.retired` (not live), and completes the log.

citation.description: The root cause (rebuild from incomplete log) is fixed by: fail-closed guard in `rebuild_source_state()`, `restore_deleted_sources()` recovering deleted events from git history, `rebuild_with_restore()` orchestrating the full repair, and `SNAPSHOT_MISSING_SOURCES` in the repairable trigger set. All verified by integration tests in test_b636_rebuild_history_loss.py.

criteria.criterion: Bug 'fsck snapshot rebuild silently drops history that exists only in a prior SNAPSHOT' is actually resolved: the reported defect no longer reproduces and expected behavior holds.
